cards.text: Friend, the two kings of Judah before this one, Manasseh and his son Amon, both did evil in the sight of the LORD (2 Kings 21:2, 20). Now Amon's son Josiah takes the throne (2 Kings 21:26). He's eight years old, and he reigns in Jerusalem thirty-one years.
His mother is Jedidah daughter of Adaiah, from Bozkath. And this young king? He does what's right in the eyes of the LORD.

cards.question: King Josiah does what's right in the eyes of the LORD. Whose ways does he walk in?

cards.text: He walks in all the ways of his ancestor King David, without turning aside to the right or to the left. He NEVER swerves, and I wobble clean across my bakery just reaching for a cookie box.

Fast forward to the eighteenth year of his reign, when King Josiah sends Shaphan, his scribe, up to the house of the LORD to have Hilkiah the high priest count the money the doorkeepers collected from the people. Friend, I lose count of sprinkles TWICE before I finish one cookie, so Hilkiah has my full respect.

cards.question: Once the money is counted, it goes to the supervisors of the work on the house of the LORD, and then to the carpenters, builders and masons. What are those workers doing?
The workmen use the money to buy ___ and dressed stone for the repairs.

cards.text: Then Josiah adds one more thing: the workers need not account for the money put into their hands. Friend, some people can't even order printer paper at work without THREE forms and a manager signing off.

cards.question: King Josiah says the workers need not account for the money, since they work with ___.
Then Hilkiah the high priest tells Shaphan the scribe he's found something in the house of the LORD. What is it?

cards.text: Hilkiah gives it to Shaphan, who reads it. Friend, NOBODY loves the word "found" more than a stamper who used to live in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Shaphan was sent about the money, and now he has a book too. When he reports to King Josiah, he talks about the book first.

cards.text: Shaphan reports the money first, and THEN he says, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." That's like burying the biggest news of the year at the bottom of a group chat about the electric bill.

cards.question: Shaphan reads the Book of the Law in the presence of King Josiah. When Josiah hears its words, he tears his clothes.

cards.text: Now the king gives a command, and it goes to five men: Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king's servant.

cards.question: King Josiah gives Hilkiah, Shaphan and the others a job about the book that's been found. What is it?

answers.text: Go and ask the LORD about it
Go and make copies of it
Go and guard it in the temple

cards.question: Josiah says the wrath of the LORD burns against them because their fathers did not obey the words of the book.

cards.text: Notice the word Josiah uses. He says the wrath burns against "us," and the king counts himself right in with everybody else.

cards.question: Hilkiah, Shaphan and the other men go to ask the LORD about the book. Who do they go to?

cards.text: Huldah is the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, the keeper of the wardrobe, and she lives in Jerusalem in the Second District. Five of the king's men walk up to her door, and I bet NOBODY wanted to be the one to knock.

Huldah opens with "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says…" and gives the LORD's message for the man who sent them. Friend, when a message starts like THAT, you put the cookie box down and you listen.

cards.question: Through Huldah, the LORD says He is about to bring calamity on this place and on its people.
The LORD says calamity is coming on this place and its people. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They forsook Him for other gods
They let His temple fall apart
They lost the Book of the Law

cards.text: They burned incense to other gods, and the LORD says His wrath will be kindled against this place and will not be quenched. Friend, that's the kind of news that makes a whole kitchen go quiet.
But then the message turns. It starts with "But as for the king of Judah…" and carries a word just for Josiah.

cards.question: The LORD says that when Josiah heard what He spoke against this place, Josiah's heart was ___.

cards.text: Josiah humbled himself, tore his clothes and wept before the LORD, and the LORD says He has heard him. That's what a tender heart looks like, friend.

cards.question: The LORD tells Josiah he will be gathered to his grave in ___.
The LORD says Josiah will see all the calamity come on this place with his own eyes.

cards.text: So the men bring Huldah's answer back to the king. Josiah has his answer now, friend, but his story is only getting STARTED.
